title: Singaporeans' Response to Situation in the Middle East
what_it_is: Singaporeans' Response to Situation in the Middle East

sections.label: Negotiated two-state solution stance
sections.summary: Singapore has consistently held for decades that only a negotiated two-state solution can deliver a comprehensive, just and durable solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This has been our consistent stance for decades.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We have also, for many years, insisted that only a negotiated two-state solution can deliver a comprehensive, just and durable solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

sections.label: Hamas attack and Israel's Gaza actions
sections.summary: Hamas's 7 October act was terrorism involving indiscriminate killing and extreme brutality, and Israel's actions in Gaza have been disproportionate and unacceptable.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: What Hamas did on 7 October was an act of terrorism that involved indiscriminate killing and extreme brutality.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Now, almost two years on, the situation has evolved greatly, and Israel's actions in Gaza have been disproportionate and unacceptable.

sections.label: Forced displacement of Palestinians
sections.summary: The continued forced displacement of Palestinians is morally reprehensible, with 1.9 million fleeing since the war began and over 750,000 since the March ceasefire.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The continued forced displacement of Palestinians is morally reprehensible, an offence against humanity.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: And 1.9 million Palestinians have had to flee their homes since the war began and since the ceasefire in March, more than 750,000.

sections.label: Singapore endorses New York Declaration
sections.summary: Earlier this month Singapore endorsed the New York Declaration at the UN General Assembly, standing firm in support of steps toward the two-state solution.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Earlier this month, Singapore endorsed the "New York Declaration" at the UN General Assembly (UNGA), once again standing firm in support of steps toward the two-state solution.

sections.label: Rallying to alleviate Palestinian suffering
sections.summary: Singaporeans are invited to rally together, act to alleviate Palestinian suffering, and remain united and constructive as one Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: She commented that Singapore always delivered what we promised.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: I invite Singaporeans to continue to rally together, speak with our actions and do what we can to alleviate the suffering of the Palestinian people.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Let us continue to be guided by wisdom and compassion, be advocates and exemplars of peace – both where the conflict is happening, and here at home with our fellow Singaporean brothers and sisters.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Let this be our compass when discussing and responding to the situation in Gaza: that whatever views we have or hold to, we will always respond constructively and responsibly, and remain united and stand together as one Singapore, even as we extend the much-needed support to those in need miles away.

sections.label: Zero tolerance for terrorism
sections.summary: Singapore has zero tolerance for terrorism, so recognising an entity holding hostages and not recognising others' right to exist is a matter of when, not if.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The second point is our zero tolerance for terrorism because of our own circumstances, so for instance, I cannot fathom or imagine trying to have diplomatic ties with an entity that is still holding hostages, that promises that it will repeat what it has done on 7 October 2023 and does not recognise the others' right to exist.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, that is why our position today is, it is not "if", but "when" to recognise, and we are waiting for that appropriate constellation of factors to be, in our view, an appropriate configuration.

sections.label: Recognition factors and targeted sanctions
sections.summary: Singapore spells out factors for when it will recognise, announces targeted sanctions, and says the situation is evolving and may require recomputing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And surely, we cannot give them cover for that.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And that is why today, what you have seen is these two announcements right, not "if", but "when", and we have spelled out the factors of when we will recognise.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The other is targeted sanctions to reflect our opposition to these violent extremist attempts to extinguish the two-state solution, and I have also added that the caveat situation is evolving very rapidly, it is unpredictable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And we will have to monitor if the situation continues to deteriorate or if Israel takes further steps to make it well-nigh impossible, we will have to recompute.

sections.label: Singapore welcomed Palestine proclamation
sections.summary: Singapore formally welcomed the proclamation of the state of Palestine 37 years ago, triggered by Arafat's rejection of terrorism, and welcomed the Palestinian Authority's continued rejection of violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Thirty-seven years ago, Singapore formally welcomed the proclamation of the state of Palestine and an important trigger for that was the explicit recognition by Yasser Arafat that the PLO would reject terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Similarly, with regard to the New York declaration, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) also welcomed the Palestinian Authority's continued rejection of violence and terrorism.

sections.label: SAF military links with Israel
sections.summary: The third question concerns the Government and SAF's extensive military-to-military links with Israel, including the joint Blue Spear missile development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The third question pertains to the Government and the Singapore Armed Forces' (SAF's) extensive military-to-military links with the state of Israel, the most recent example of this being the joint development of a surface-to-surface missile Blue Spear by Singapore Technologies and the Israel Aerospace Industries.

sections.label: Threat assessment from Singapore-Israel ties
sections.summary: The question asks for the current threat assessment to Singapore and its interests from radicalised individuals abroad and self-radicalised individuals locally over perceived close Singapore-Israel ties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What is the current threat assessment to Singapore and Singapore interests arising from a perception of close Singapore-Israel ties from radicalised individuals abroad and self-radicalised individuals locally?

sections.label: Position is not if but when
sections.summary: The speaker caveated that the position is not if but when, and that further deterioration or Israeli action extinguishing a two-state solution would require reconsidering the position.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: That is why I have also caveated that our position is not if, but when.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We have also highlighted that if the situation continues to deteriorate or if Israel takes further action to extinguish any prospect for a two-state solution, then we have to reconsider our position.

sections.label: Recognise Palestinian state conditions
sections.summary: Singapore will recognise the Palestinian state when there is an effective government renouncing terrorism and recognising the state of Israel.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Today, I am telling you we will recognise the Palestinian state when there is effective government renouncing terrorism, recognising the state of Israel.

sections.label: Assurance not being held hostage
sections.summary: The speaker gives an assurance that they are not being held hostage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, I am not going to go into that area.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But I give you this assurance that we are not being held hostage.

sections.label: Evidence on radicalisation relationship
sections.summary: The question asks whether MHA has evidence that the close relationship contributes to heightened radicalisation faced by Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Is there any evidence that MHA has that the close relationship contributes to a heightened environment of radicalisation faced by Singapore?

sections.label: Gaza war, sanctions, small states
sections.summary: Singaporeans are anguished by the Gaza war and ask about tougher sanctions, Singapore's role for small states, and erosion of international rules.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Number one, Singaporeans, including our residents in Tampines, are saddened and anguished by the war in Gaza.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: They wonder whether the Government can take further actions, including tougher sanctions, to demonstrate Singapore's objection towards the atrocities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Small countries like ours rely on international law for survival.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: How does the Ministry see Singapore's role in speaking up for other small entities or states when injustice occurs and what does the erosion of international rules in this conflict signal for the security of small states like ours?

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: This is in fact the first time we are imposing sanctions.

sections.label: Two-state solution assessment
sections.summary: The expression reflects the assessment that the situation is wrong and that a two-state solution is the only viable way forward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: This is an expression that is in keeping with our assessment of the situation, that it is wrong and it is inimical to the long-term interests of both Palestinians and Israel.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: It is a reflection that we continue to believe a two-state solution is the only viable way forward.

sections.label: Guarding national interest
sections.summary: The speaker says national interest must be guarded jealously, defined here as unity, security and support for international law.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Next, we need to guard jealously our national interest and, I have told you, in this case, our national interest is unity, security and support for international law for what it is worth, despite all the limitations that it has.

sections.label: Evidence they can and have
sections.summary: The speaker states that they can and have, and that evidence of them has been seen.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Of course, they can and they have and we have seen evidence of them.

sections.label: Israel genocide call and aid
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will call Israel out for genocide and outlines 10 tranches of humanitarian assistance by airdrop or land.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the Government call Israel out for committing genocide?

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I have outlined our 10 tranches of humanitarian assistance, whether by airdrop or by supplies delivered over land.

sections.label: Genocide left to ICJ
sections.summary: The passage states the genocide question would be left to be determined by the International Court of Justice.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: On genocide, as I said earlier in the Statement, I would leave this to be determined by the International Court of Justice.

sections.label: Sanctions not entered lightly
sections.summary: The passage states that sanctions are not something entered into lightly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Sanctions are not something we enter into lightly.

sections.label: Sanctions impact not overstated
sections.summary: The passage says sanctions were not entered into lightly but their impact should not be overstated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, I am not saying that we entered into sanctions lightly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But I do not want to overstate its impact.

sections.label: Minister visit and SAF airdrops
sections.summary: The passage describes a 2024 visit to the United Arab Emirates, Egypt, Palestinian territories and Israel, and SAF C-130 airdrops with the Jordanian air force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Minister gained access to the United Arab Emirates, Egypt, Palestinian territories and Israel, all in the same visit, in 2024, and were able to listen to many different levels of positions and each level not being homogenous.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Also, the second level of agency, which is our SAF, being able to deploy our Charlie-130s airdrops, working with the Jordanian air force.

sections.label: Sanctions and two-state solution
sections.summary: The passage asks how proposed sanctions would move the needle on peace and a two-state solution given extreme views on both sides.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How do we expect the proposed sanctions to move the needle on peace and desired outcomes, including a two-state solution, given the very extreme views on both sides, as mentioned by the Minister, including members of the Israeli government who have rejected the two-state solution, not just political activists or settlers in the West Bank, by vowing to destroy Gaza?

sections.label: Open lines of communication
sections.summary: The Minister said open lines of communication with both ends are maintained and important in peace and crisis, and asks if they could support ceasefire negotiations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Minister also mentioned how we have consistently maintained open lines of communication with both ends and that this is important, not just in times of peace, but also during times of crisis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, will the Government thus consider using these open lines of communication to support perhaps ceasefire negotiations, in some shape or form, more directly beyond the humanitarian assistance?

sections.label: US leverage in Middle East
sections.summary: The speaker says the last two years show the US is the single superpower with real leverage in the Middle East, depending on decisions in Washington.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: As far as I am concerned, what the last two years have illustrated is that, actually, the single superpower with real leverage in the Middle East, is the US.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Depending on those decisions made in Washington, which will also reflect its own complex domestic political situation, that is where real leverage may or may not be applied to bring, at least an interim ceasefire, hopefully, a permanent ceasefire and the release of all hostages.

sections.label: Singapore condemns Qatar sovereignty violation
sections.summary: The speaker says MFA condemned the attack as an egregious violation of Qatar's sovereignty, a core principle Singapore staunchly supports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: The Ministerial Statements did not quite answer my question, but I know MFA put out a statement, condemning the attack and stating that it is an egregious violation of Qatar's sovereignty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: So, given that Singapore has been a staunch supporter of this core principle of respect of the sovereignty of all nations, big and small, not just any piece of international law but of this very core principle of international law, because it is fundamental to our survival as a small state and therefore, Singapore has also responded robustly to other instances of the violation of sovereignty of other nations by other nations in the past, going beyond verbal condemnation, imposing sanctions.

sections.label: Reserving response for egregious issues
sections.summary: The speaker is not inclined to go further, preferring to reserve response for the most egregious and important issues.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Having said that, I think the Member is asking whether we should go further.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I am not inclined to do further because, otherwise, we will end up having to chase every and every infraction which countries are engaged in against each other and us having to respond.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, my preference is to reserve it for the most egregious, the most important issues where we need to make a point.

sections.label: Zero tolerance for terrorism
sections.summary: The speaker urges everyone to return to zero-tolerance for breach of international law, terrorism, and any justifications or pretext for terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Can we again, I want to persuade everyone, to come back to the zero-tolerance for breach of international law and zero-tolerance for terrorism and zero-tolerance, therefore, for even accepting any justifications or pretext for terrorism and harbouring them.

sections.label: Watch how things unfold
sections.summary: The speaker declines to re-evaluate the position and says to watch carefully how things unfold in days, weeks and months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The Member is already jumping and asking me to re-evaluate our position.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I would say, let us watch very, very carefully how things unfold in the days, weeks and months.

sections.label: Israeli and Palestinian state existence
sections.summary: The speaker says both the Israeli state and the Palestinian state deserve to exist.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I do not know whether it means I obviously have not been able to communicate effectively or maybe this is a chance for me to reiterate the key points.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We believe both the Israeli state and the Palestinian state deserve to exist.

sections.label: Humanitarian aid and conditional recognition
sections.summary: Singapore will extend humanitarian assistance as collective compassion, leading to conditional recognition for Palestine.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We will do our best to extend humanitarian assistance as a real expression of the collective compassion of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: That is why today, we have reached this point of conditional recognition for Palestine.

sections.label: UN resolution vote rationale
sections.summary: Singapore voted for the 19 September UN resolution on Palestine's participation because it calls out 7 October, hostages, ceasefire and a Palestinian state.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I would like the Minister for Foreign Affairs to explain the rationale behind Singapore voting for the recent UN resolution on 19 September calling for the participation of Palestine at the opening of the 80th session of the UN General Assembly while still withholding the recognition of a Palestinian state.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We voted in favour of the resolution because if you read the resolution in its entirety, you will see that it is a comprehensive one, which I would say, makes many countries who voted for it, there will be parts which they agree, there will be parts which they disagree.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But it is one of the few, or one of the fewer UN resolutions that actually calls out 7 October as a terrorist act committed by Hamas that calls for the immediate release of hostages, also calls for immediate ceasefire and also calls ultimately for a state of Palestine to take its place in the UN.
